The checker rejected the program because the word "input" appeared in comments, such as "Input pair". It searches the program text for forbidden names, so those comments now say "differential pair" instead. The circuit, sizing and predictions are unchanged. It is still a two-stage Miller op-amp with an NMOS diff pair, PMOS mirror load, PMOS common-source second stage and an Rz–Cc compensation network.

```python
PARAMS = {
    "gmid1": (14.0, 8.0, 20.0),      # diff pair gm/Id
    "L1":    (0.5, 0.15, 1.5),       # diff pair L
    "I1":    (22e-6, 8e-6, 40e-6),   # current per pair device (tail = 2*I1)
    "gmid3": (11.0, 6.0, 15.0),      # PMOS mirror load and M6 gm/Id (matched)
    "L3":    (0.5, 0.3, 1.5),        # PMOS load and M6 L (matched)
    "I6":    (240e-6, 100e-6, 300e-6),  # second-stage current
    "gmidb": (10.0, 6.0, 14.0),      # NMOS bias mirrors gm/Id
    "Lb":    (1.0, 0.5, 2.0),        # NMOS bias mirrors L
    "Cc":    (0.6e-12, 0.2e-12, 2e-12),
    "rzk":   (2.0, 0.5, 6.0),        # Rz = rzk / gm6
}

def design(p, lut, spec):
    cl = spec.get("cl", 2e-12)
    iref = spec.get("iref", 10e-6)
    vdd = 1.8
    I1 = p["I1"]; Itail = 2 * I1; I6 = p["I6"]; Cc = p["Cc"]

    # Bias network: ibias diode, tail source, second-stage sink (same gm/Id and L)
    m0 = lut.size("n", p["gmidb"], p["Lb"], iref, vds=0.65)
    m5 = lut.size("n", p["gmidb"], p["Lb"], Itail, vds=0.3)
    m7 = lut.size("n", p["gmidb"], p["Lb"], I6, vds=0.9)

    # Differential pair
    m1 = lut.size("n", p["gmid1"], p["L1"], I1, vds=0.4, vsb=0.3)
    # PMOS mirror load (diode side vds = vsg)
    m3 = lut.size("p", p["gmid3"], p["L3"], I1, vds=1.0)
    m4 = lut.size("p", p["gmid3"], p["L3"], I1, vds=m3.vgs)
    # Second stage PMOS CS: same gm/Id and L as M4 -> no systematic offset
    m6 = lut.size("p", p["gmid3"], p["L3"], I6, vds=0.9)

    gm6 = m6.gm
    Rz = p["rzk"] / gm6

    n = Netlist("vinp vinn vout vdd vss ibias")
    n.dev("M0", "ibias", "ibias", "vss", "vss", m0)
    n.dev("M5", "tail", "ibias", "vss", "vss", m5)
    # vinn on diode side, vinp on output side: stage 1 inverts from vinp,
    # stage 2 inverts again -> vout non-inverting w.r.t. vinp.
    n.dev("M1", "d1", "vinn", "tail", "vss", m1)
    n.dev("M2", "o1", "vinp", "tail", "vss", m1)
    n.dev("M3", "d1", "d1", "vdd", "vdd", m3)
    n.dev("M4", "o1", "d1", "vdd", "vdd", m4)
    n.dev("M6", "vout", "o1", "vdd", "vdd", m6)
    n.dev("M7", "vout", "ibias", "vss", "vss", m7)
    n.R("Rz", "o1", "cz", Rz)
    n.C("Cc", "cz", "vout", Cc)

    # Predictions
    gm1 = m1.gm
    a1 = gm1 / (m1.gds + m4.gds)
    a2 = gm6 / (m6.gds + m7.gds)
    gain_db = db(a1 * a2)
    ugbw = gm1 / (2 * PI * Cc)
    C1 = m6.cgg + m4.cdd + m1.cdd + m4.cgd
    C2 = cl + m6.cdd + m7.cdd
    p2 = gm6 * Cc / (C1 * Cc + C2 * Cc + C1 * C2) / (2 * PI)
    if Rz > 1.0 / gm6:
        z = 1.0 / (2 * PI * Cc * (Rz - 1.0 / gm6))
        zph = math.degrees(math.atan(ugbw / z))
    else:
        zph = 0.0
    p3 = 1.0 / (2 * PI * Rz * C1)
    m3pole = m3.gm / (2 * PI * 2 * m3.cgg)
    pm = 90 - math.degrees(math.atan(ugbw / p2)) + zph \
         - math.degrees(math.atan(ugbw / p3)) \
         - math.degrees(math.atan(ugbw / m3pole)) * 0.5
    power = vdd * (iref + Itail + I6)
    slew = min(Itail / Cc, I6 / (cl + Cc))
    swing = vdd - m6.vdsat - m7.vdsat - 0.1

    return n, {"gain_db": gain_db, "ugbw": ugbw, "pm": pm, "power": power,
               "slew": slew, "swing": swing, "polarity": 1}
```

At the starting values, my hand estimates are about 529 µW total power and an unity-gain bandwidth of about 82 MHz. Slew is about 73 V/µs, set by the first stage. DC gain is the spec most at risk. With L = 0.5 µm in both stages, 65 dB may be tight. If the simulation comes in short, the refiner can raise `L1` and `L3`.
